notes.title: Development Update: Entering Phase 2: Stripping down to the core
notes.notes:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2][p]In my last post I promised to cover the narrative and the emotional core I hope Selve can express, but I have to talk about this first, the next one will cover that, I promise[/p][p]I wanted to share a big update on the direction of the project and where things are headed next. Over the past year (from April 2024 to April 2025), I’ve been building an internal demo full of experiments, features, and systems. This was an important phase where I let myself explore freely, trying out different ideas to figure out what this game truly wanted to be.[/p][p]Through that process, I was able to define the [b]theme[/b], [b]story[/b], and [b]worldbuilding[/b] of Selve. I also learned which mechanics actually serve the heart of the experience and which ones just get in the way.[/p][p]The core theme I want to communicate is:[/p][p]"How can I express different emotions or ideas through a melody?"[/p][p][/p][p]Now that the development of this game is moving to the next stage, some initial decisions need to be refined and discarded: this is Design by Subtraction.[/p][p]That means cutting out everything that doesn’t align with the theme. It’s time to refine.[/p][p][/p][h2]What’s Changing?[/h2][p][/p][p]In the current version of the game, you manipulate NPCs using music-composing magic. It’s an interesting system, but too complex, and it ended up pulling the game away from that core theme. The process of influencing NPCs took too many steps and wasn’t really that fun. So I'm removing that whole system.[/p][p]Also, platforming.
There’s still going to be some, after all, exploration is part of the experience, but it’s no longer a main pillar of the game. It’ll be there to support the world, not distract from the music.[/p][p][/p][h2]What’s the New Focus?[/h2][p]The game is now about [b]simply playing melodies[/b].
You’ll perform them for the [b]giant spirits[/b] of the [b]Mulong tribe[/b], who will judge your songs based on their own unique preferences. If they like your melody, they’ll reward you.[/p][p]This mechanic, which I briefly explored during the development of the first internal demo, uses a machine learning algorithm called a [b]Support Vector Machine[/b]. This algorithm allows each giant spirit to be trained with songs it likes. For example, let's say the first spirit, a giant turtle, loves chill melodies. I'll train it with what I consider chill melodies. Each giant spirit will teach the player some aspect of music creation and how it affects the emotion it evokes.[/p][p][/p][p]I'm planning on allowing players to train those giant spirits in what they think would be best for each one, for example, if you feel that the chill music that the turtle should like is a fast-paced melody (for some reason) with very random jumps in the melody and such, then you could train it! And then share your training data with other players so they can play Selve under your vision of how the music evokes emotions.

As I said, I'm starting this process right now, so I have some videos I can share with you, this are early attempts to prove this makes sense and that it's fun, keep that in mind!

[/p][previewyoutube="nKtYinV4hH8;full"][/previewyoutube][p]This is Doco, the giant tortoise, the spirit of calm.[/p][p]Doco isn't reacting to what you play yet, this is a test to show that the action will produce good enough music, this test is trying to consider how minimal the background music should be, whether the synth tone and background blend well, etc. I'm happy with the results so far, so I'm moving forward and in the next few weeks I'll implement this change, making the spirit judge and react to what you play.[/p][p][/p][h2]What's next?[/h2][p]I’m now working on a [b]lean demo[/b], focused only on what I think matters in this game. This new demo will be a much tighter experience that showcases the core idea behind Selve. I'm working hard on this demo (while applying for public tenders for funding) so I can share it here, so stay tuned for future updates.[/p][p]
I hope you like the changes I'm making to the game! I think this is the right direction for the project, let me know what you think!

Cheers!
Nico Frois[/p]

notes.title: Why make this game?
notes.notes:
[h1]Because music is much deeper than just rhythm[/h1]

[b]The short answer:[/b] because I feel that video games, in general, have stopped exploring mechanics centered around music. Most [b]music games today are just rhythm games[/b]. I have nothing against them, but for me, [b]music holds many interesting aspects worth exploring[/b]. I’d like to dedicate my life to uncovering the different elements that fascinate me. In this case, Selve focuses on melody—seeking answers to questions like: What makes a melody sound good? How can I make what I play sound pleasing? How can I express different emotions or ideas through a melody?

But where does this curiosity come from? Mainly, from a deep desire to understand the world of musical creation and to bring that world closer to others. This is the core principle behind this game—and, hopefully, the ones I will continue to develop in the future. At least when it comes to gameplay mechanics.

I can't end this post without mentioning the two games that have influenced me the most. Their influence might not be immediately obvious in Selve, but they are undeniably a big reason why I'm now making music-focused games: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Donkey Kong Jungle Beat (with the bongo controllers!).

[list]
[*]Ocarina of Time was such a creative and inspiring adventure for me. I played it when I was around 17—not exactly a little kid—but I was deeply into music at the time, learning guitar and getting into music theory. That Zelda game arrived at just the right moment in my life. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45594991/6204c92bb572a974f950a661ec3b05fca9fce735.png[/img]
[*]When I played Donkey Kong Jungle Beat, it was another eye-opening moment. It made me realize that game controls didn’t have to be just a joystick—the type of control you use shapes the experience itself. That game offered a far more physical experience, and the battles were genuinely intense in a bodily, energetic way.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45594991/55d3eecfd8719f5a4c83a7e59dd00e4e7f1aea05.jpg[/img]
[/list]

These influences have stayed with me throughout my life. I think I even studied Electronic Engineering just so I could learn how to make controls like the ones in Donkey Kong. And while I haven't yet created something quite as intense, I like to think I’ve been exploring how a music game can be controlled. Selve can be played with a keyboard, a joystick, a MIDI controller, a microphone with a real instrument or your voice—and I’ve even tested it with a dance mat (great workout, by the way! haha).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45594991/f055db30fcd5121948f67445c781924429f648fd.png[/img]

Thanks to everyone who read this far—I know it was a lot of information, but I wanted to share it here, in what I hope will be my first major game.
The next post will be about the narrative and the emotional core I hope Selve can express.

Cheers!
Nico Frois
